findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the user_data script, which is stored in Terraform state and accessible via the EC2 instance metadata service, exposing long-lived AWS credentials to anyone with access to the instance or state file.
The security group allows inbound SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the management port to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks.
The security group allows inbound HTTP (port 80) from 0.0.0.0/0 with no compensating controls such as TLS termination or WAF, exposing the web application unencrypted to the public internet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a kms_key_id, meaning data stored on this attached disk is unencrypted at rest.

The S3 bucket used to store VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration (aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration), leaving potentially sensitive network traffic logs unencrypted at rest.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy is defined for the bucket, and force_destroy is enabled, so the bucket could be left with default or overly permissive access allowing exposure or accidental destruction of flow log data.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing the internet-facing attack surface.
map_public_ip_on_launch is set to true, automatically assigning public IP addresses to any instance launched in this subnet, increasing the internet-facing attack surface.

The EBS snapshot inherits from an unencrypted source volume, so the snapshot itself is unencrypted, and no encryption settings are applied, risking exposure of disk data if the snapshot is shared or accessed improperly.
